diagnostic_evidence.quote:
X:= H^2(0,T; H^{-1}(\Omega))
\cap L^2(0,T; \HozOmega)
\cap H^1(0,T; L^2(\Omega)),

issues.failure_explanation: L²-in-time H⁻¹ forcing does not generally produce the asserted energy regularity. On (0,π), with zero initial data, take f(t,x)=Σj sin(jt)sin(jx). This belongs to L²(H⁻¹), but its modal solution has u′j(t)=t sin(jt)/2, so u′ is not in L²(L²). Thus the solution need not belong to X.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the already adopted assumption f∈L²(0,T;L²(Ω)) before asserting well-posedness in X.
issues.overall_effect: The initial well-posedness claim covers a forcing class larger than the stated solution space permits; the subsequent stronger forcing assumption avoids this obstruction.
issues.title: The initial forcing class does not give well-posedness in the stated space
issues.why_classification: This local restriction uses an assumption already imposed for the rest of the paper and changes no subsequent method, estimate, or advertised convergence rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
the linear system to solve is square
(which entails that existence is equivalent to uniqueness).

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed set is not a vector space when dim(Vh)>1: for independent a,b∈Vh, the polynomial a+tb is not generally a single separated product. Testing with all separated functions imposes the full tensor-product equations by linearity, while the stated trial set remains rank-restricted. Consequently, generic loads need not have a trial solution, and the asserted square linear system is not the system defined by these spaces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the tensor product as the linear span of separated products, equivalently as all sums Σj=0^p t^j vj with vj∈Vh.
issues.overall_effect: The fully discrete construction and its general solvability claim are not valid for the trial set actually defined.
issues.title: The defined tensor-product trial set contains only rank-one functions
issues.why_classification: Replacing the rank-one set by the standard finite-dimensional tensor product is a local, routine construction correction that restores the intended scheme and unknown count.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The initial condition~$\uzeroh$ is imposed strongly in~$\Xh$;

issues.failure_explanation: Neither braced space requires its functions to vanish at t=0. Even with the intended full tensor-product interpretation, adding u0,h to this space does not impose uh(0)=u0,h. The first slab therefore has an unfixed displacement, contrary to the square-system and initial-error arguments. The same defect occurs in Xτ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the functions in both braced trial spaces to have zero trace at t=0, or explicitly impose uh(0)=u0,h and uτ(0)=u0 in the formulations.
issues.overall_effect: As defined, both schemes lack the prescribed displacement condition, and estimates that discard the corresponding initial error are unsupported.
issues.title: The trial spaces do not enforce the initial displacement
issues.why_classification: Adding the intended initial trace condition is a routine local repair and preserves all substantive schemes and guarantees.

for all $n=1,\dots,N$.
Let $\Pizpbftmo$ denote the piecewise $L^2$ projector onto~$\Pbb_{\pnt-1}(\In;L^2(\Omega))$

issues.failure_explanation: An L²-orthogonal projector onto polynomials with H¹₀ spatial coefficients is not defined for arbitrary L²-valued f, because that range is not closed in the stated L² norm. For time-constant f=g with g∈L²\H¹₀, orthogonality against all H¹₀ coefficients would force the projected coefficient to equal g, outside the declared range.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the L²(Ω)-valued temporal projector, as the stability proof subsequently does; retain H¹₀-valued functions only as the test functions.
issues.overall_effect: The semidiscrete right-hand-side rewrite is undefined under its initial projector definition.
issues.title: The initial time projector has an inadmissible spatial range
issues.why_classification: The source already supplies the appropriate projector later, so correcting this range requires no new argument or change of estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: An arbitrary real Banach space has no specified inner product (·,·)X. The orthogonality definitions, the lemma's identity, and later identifications of squared norms with such pairings are therefore undefined at the advertised level of generality. A Banach-valued moment construction would require a different definition and justification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State these inner-product-based results for real Hilbert spaces. This includes every spatial space used in the actual error analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The general Banach-space projection and reconstruction statements are not established as written.
issues.title: The projection and reconstruction results use inner products on arbitrary Banach spaces
issues.why_classification: A standard ambient-space condition removes an unused generality while preserving all actual applications, constructions, and rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The global assumptions allow p1=1. On I1=[0,1], w=t² then requires an affine integrated projector to take values 0 and 1 and have derivative 2 at 1, which is impossible. Thus the claimed equivalent definition used by the lemma is not defined in an allowed case. Independently downstream, the reconstruction proof uses a linear test unavailable when p1−1=0; its endpoint value matching fails for a nonzero initial velocity jump.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Then, for all~$w$ in $H^{s+1}(\In;\mathcal X)$
with $s\geq0$,

issues.failure_explanation: The unrestricted s is incompatible with a right-hand side containing only the derivative of order s+1. For degree p, take s=p+1 and w=t^(p+1). The displayed right-hand side is zero because w^(p+2)=0, although no degree-p approximant can equal w. The same uncapped-seminorm defect propagates to the integrated operator and the smooth-data estimates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the approximation estimates only up to the effective polynomial regularity and cap the derivative order accordingly, or replace the offending seminorms by suitable full Sobolev norms. Propagate that correction through the convergence theorem.
issues.overall_effect: Several polynomial-approximation estimates and the resulting high-regularity error bounds are false with their stated seminorm dependence.
issues.title: Saturated approximation rates retain an impossibly high derivative seminorm
issues.why_classification: This is a limited weakening of the asserted seminorm estimates. The convergence exponents can survive, but the claimed regularity dependence must be revised throughout the affected estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: On the first slab, integration by parts gives ∫(ΠhEu−PΠhEu)″q=((PΠhEu)′(0)−ΠhEu1,q(0)). Consequently, the projected function's fictitious left velocity must be ΠhEu1 for the displayed forcing fξ to be correct. The stability data for ξ are therefore ΠhEu1−u1,h, not (PΠhEu)′(0)−u1,h. The latter is the actual right derivative and generally differs from ΠhEu1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the left velocity ΠhEu1−u1,h consistently. Bound its spatial projection error by the already included projected initial term plus the endpoint estimate for (I−ΠhE)u; the resulting τ1/p1-weighted u″ residual is absorbed by the existing residual contribution.
issues.overall_effect: The first-slab error equation and the subsequent stability application are not consistent with one another.
issues.title: The error equation and stability estimate use inconsistent initial velocities
issues.why_classification: The source already provides the endpoint estimate and residual term needed for a local re-estimation, so the lemma's substantive bound and downstream rates can be preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We recall that~$\uzeroh$ is the elliptic projection of~$\uzero$

issues.failure_explanation: For degree-px conforming elements, the saturated H¹ approximation order is h^px, not h^(px+1). For example, the piecewise-linear Ritz projection of x(1−x) on a uniform one-dimensional mesh has H¹ error proportional to h, whereas the displayed bound gives h² for sufficiently large s.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the initial discretization actually selected, bypass this estimate: ξh(0)=ΠhEu0−u0,h=0 exactly. Remove its contribution before estimating ξh; the nonnegative initial term may remain in the final bound harmlessly.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted estimate of gimel1 is false, so that step of the hp proof cannot be used.
issues.title: The initial Ritz projection is assigned one extra spatial order
issues.why_classification: The source-supported zero-initial-projection-error bypass preserves the stated overall bound and convergence rates without a replacement argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The spatial Ritz error is independent of pkt. With h and px fixed, choose u(t)=tw for a smooth w∉Vh and increase pkt. The temporal projection is exact, so ρ′=(I−ΠhE)w remains nonzero, whereas the asserted gimel7 bound tends to zero through the factors involving pkt. The spatial approximation factors must depend on px.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-estimate the spatial part with px, using h^(2 min(s,px)+2)/px^(2s+2) and its elliptic-regularity correction, and revise the theorem's corresponding term.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed separate dependence on spatial and temporal polynomial degrees is incorrect. The isotropic specialization px=pkt does not exhibit this particular defect.
issues.title: A spatial projection error is bounded using the temporal polynomial degree
issues.why_classification: The independent-degree guarantee must be changed, but a contained spatial approximation correction preserves the method and the convergence framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
All other~$\gimel_j$ terms, $j=1,2,4,5,6,8$,
already gave $\mathcal O(\tau^\p)$ rates.

issues.failure_explanation: For α=1, h=τ, fixed p, and s≤p, the accumulated gimel5 and gimel6 bounds have size O(τ^(s−1)), not O(τ^(s−1/2)). Their sums of squared local L² norms form global norms and supply no extra τ^(1/2). Nor is tm assumed to be O(τ). The smooth-case local L∞ argument in the proof does not establish the finite-regularity branch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace this branch by the O(τ^(s−1)) rate supported by the displayed bounds, with the parent theorem's actual regularity requirements. Retaining the stated half-order improvement requires an additional argument controlling the accumulated residuals.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimal finite-regularity rate is not proved by the theorem from which the corollary is claimed to follow.
issues.title: The finite-regularity corollary gains an unsupported half order
issues.why_classification: The source-supported resolution materially worsens the central convergence rate in the finite-regularity regime; no source argument recovers the promised half order.

issues.failure_explanation: A time polynomial with an L²-valued Laplacian has all its spatial coefficients, including its initial value, in the Laplacian's L² domain. The stated assumption on u does not impose that on u0. For example, on (0,π), u=Σj j^(−9/4)e^(−jt)sin(jx) has Δu and f=u″−Δu in L²(L²), with the stated basic initial regularity, but u0∉H². No time-polynomial approximation matching that u0 can have Δuτ∈L²(L²).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume discrete Laplacian regularity separately, or add u0 to the L² domain of the Dirichlet Laplacian and establish the resulting slabwise regularity using the projected discrete equation.
issues.overall_effect: The weaker standing a posteriori assumption does not ensure that the discrete Laplacian quantities in the estimator exist. The stronger sufficient assumptions on u0 avoid this counterexample.
issues.title: Space-time regularity of the exact Laplacian does not imply discrete Laplacian regularity
issues.why_classification: The claimed weaker data scope must be restricted or supplemented, but the stronger data regime already presented in the paper supports a comparable analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the equation gives u‴=Δu′+f′, but the assumptions only make f′ square integrable in time. Take a smooth Dirichlet eigenfunction φ and u(t,x)=t^(11/4)φ(x), with f defined by the equation. Both initial data are zero and f∈H¹(L²), yet u‴ is proportional to t^(−1/4)φ and is not in L∞(H⁻¹).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace W³,∞(H⁻¹) by H³(H⁻¹), or state W³,∞ only under an additional essentially bounded forcing-derivative assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The strongest asserted time-regularity component is false; the lower regularity needed for Δu∈L²(L²) is not defeated by this counterexample.
issues.title: H¹ forcing does not imply an essentially bounded third time derivative
issues.why_classification: A substantive regularity conclusion must be weakened, but the comparable lower-regularity result and its a posteriori applications remain available.

issues.failure_explanation: The general first-derivative-only approximation inequality invoked here is false at this constant. On an interval of length τ, a smooth unit-Lipschitz zigzag can alternate between ±a at p+2 equally spaced points, with a arbitrarily close to τ/[2(p+1)]. Every degree-p polynomial then has uniform error at least a, since a smaller error forces p+1 distinct zeros. For p≥8 this exceeds τ/[π(p−2)]. Multiplication by a fixed unit spatial function gives the same obstruction in L²(Ω). No special restriction on the error-generated v is proved that would justify the smaller constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove and use a valid explicit Hilbert-valued Jackson-kernel estimate with a larger constant, for example a bound 400τ/(p+1) times the Lipschitz norm, and propagate the replacement through c3, c4, the estimator, and oscillation.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical constants used in the constant-free reliability estimates are not justified.
issues.title: The explicit Lipschitz approximation constant is too small
issues.why_classification: A contained nontrivial approximation lemma and recalibration of constants are required, but the 1/p scaling and the global reliability proof architecture can be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we get the following identity in~$L^2(\In;L^2(\Omega))$:

issues.failure_explanation: At n=1 the displayed jump contains Δuτ′(0+)−Δu1. The assumptions only put u1 in H¹₀, so Δu1 need not be in L². For example, zero u0 and f together with u1∈H¹₀\H² satisfy the stated assumptions on a convex interval. Although the discrete polynomial coefficients have L² Laplacians, the initial jump does not. The reconstruction also inherits u1, so ΔRuτ and the claimed L² error equation are not justified on the first slab.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require u1 to belong to the L² domain of the Dirichlet Laplacian, which on the stipulated convex domains is ensured by u1∈H²∩H¹₀. Otherwise the first-slab reconstruction contribution needs a different, weaker-norm estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The estimator can be undefined for data expressly allowed by the reliability proposition.
issues.title: The reliability estimator requires an unassumed Laplacian of the initial velocity
issues.why_classification: An additional spatial regularity requirement on one initial datum gives a comparable result without changing the estimator's rates or the global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We construct a computable error estimator
\item Find the interval index $m$ where $\eta_1$ attains the maximum and set $\xi = t_{m-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: η2 and oscillation depend on the slab containing the maximum of the unknown reconstructed error, so the displayed η is not a computable a posteriori quantity as defined. Neither choosing m=N nor maximizing the jump-based η1 establishes that condition. Candidate bounds are not monotone in m: moving a slab from the final position to an earlier position reduces its residual weight from τn to τn c3/π. The adaptive choice can also set ξ=0 when m=1, although the reconstructed error there is zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Eliminate the unknown index by taking the maximum, over every candidate final slab, of the complete η2-plus-oscillation expression, retaining the separate maximum defining η1. Update localization and marking to represent this computable bound rather than substituting a jump-maximizing slab.
issues.overall_effect: The formal error-dependent bound does not certify the estimator actually computed in the uniform or adaptive experiments.
issues.title: The estimator retains an unknown error-maximizing slab
issues.why_classification: A finite reoptimization and corresponding localization change are needed, but the source's candidate bounds provide a complete route to a computable estimator without new global proof architecture.
